selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: Why does the traveler begin a new journey with his intellect?
questions.answer: He wants to look for clear signs that show Allah is One.

questions.question: Where do the traveler and his intellect stop first?
questions.answer: They arrive at the first stopping-place in their new search.

questions.question: What do they see at that first stopping-place?
questions.answer: They see four holy and clear truths spread across the whole universe.

questions.question: What do those four truths prove?
questions.answer: They prove the unity of Allah.

questions.question: In this passage, what was the traveler’s earlier goal in being sent to the world?
questions.answer: It was to reach faith.

questions.question: How had the traveler searched before this new journey?
questions.answer: He had traveled through the universe in his mind, asking creation about its Creator.

questions.question: What level of certainty had the traveler already reached before starting this new journey?
questions.answer: He had reached certainty about the Necessary Existence of his Creator.

questions.question: What does the phrase about the truths “prevailing over the whole cosmos” suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that these signs are universal, not limited to one place or one group of things.

questions.question: What can we infer about the role of the intellect in this passage?
questions.answer: The intellect is being used as a companion in thinking, reflecting, and recognizing the proofs.

questions.question: How clear are these truths said to be?
questions.answer: They are described as plainly showing the unity of Allah.

questions.question: Who is the main person described in the passage?
questions.answer: A traveler seeking true faith and certainty about Allah.

questions.question: What had this traveler been asking throughout the universe?
questions.answer: He had been asking everything about its Maker.

questions.question: What was he trying to find in every place?
questions.answer: He was trying to find his Lord, Allah.

questions.question: After reaching certainty about Necessary Existence, what new goal does he choose?
questions.answer: He chooses to search for proofs that Allah is One.

questions.question: Whom does the traveler speak to before beginning the new journey?
questions.answer: He speaks to his intellect.

questions.question: How many sacred truths are seen at the first stopping-place?
questions.answer: Four.

questions.question: How are those truths described in relation to the cosmos?
questions.answer: They are described as ruling or appearing over the whole universe.

questions.question: What kind of proof do these truths give about Allah’s unity?
questions.answer: They give proof that is obvious and strong.

questions.question: Why is the first stopping-place important in the passage?
questions.answer: It begins the next part of the traveler’s search by showing broad signs of tawhid.

questions.question: What do these truths make clear?
questions.answer: They make clear that Allah’s unity is certain.

questions.question: What title is given to this section of the passage?
questions.answer: It is about proofs of Divine unity.

questions.question: Why is the traveler described as someone sent to the world to attain faith?
questions.answer: It shows that faith is a major purpose of his life and journey.

questions.question: What method did the traveler use to explore the cosmos?
questions.answer: He traveled through it in his mind.

questions.question: What had the traveler already found with complete certainty before this part begins?
questions.answer: He had found certainty that the Creator necessarily exists.
